findings.claim: scripts/wp_scp_022_gate_check.sh does not implement the 3× APPROVED hash-chain verification that §4.7 item 2 requires and that the script's own header claims closes R1 CRIT-BYPASS-003.
findings.evidence: §4.7 enumerates four checks the helper performs; item 2 is: '3× APPROVED hash chain — For each merged slice, verify fixpoint.md contains hash-chain entries over the three reviewer JSONs and that the hash chain reproduces.' The script header (lines 5–11) echoes this claim: 'Closes WP-SCP-022 R1 CRIT-BYPASS-003 (3× APPROVED has no hard-stop).' Inspection of the complete script (213 lines) finds no check_fixpoint_hash_chain function and no --fixpoint or --check-hash-chain mode. The --slice dispatch path (main() lines 184–188) calls only check_no_symlink_escape, check_d021_collision, and check_acc_pin. The --gate path calls only check_gate_artefact. A grep for 'hash' in the script body returns only the comment at line 6 — no implementation. The hash-chain verification is entirely absent from the script.
findings.impact: The gate helper is the primary machine enforcement for the 'no merge without 3× APPROVED' invariant (D-026; §2 invariant 1). §4.5 credits fixpoint.md plus the gate helper together for the partial CRIT-BYPASS-003 closure. Without the hash-chain verification step in the script, fixpoint.md can be created by the orchestrator but is never verified by any machine check before the next slice is dispatched. A tampered, malformed, or orchestrator-hallucinated fixpoint.md would pass the gate silently. The plan's claimed partial closure of CRIT-BYPASS-003 at the gate-helper level does not exist in the implementation.
findings.mitigation: Add a check_fixpoint_hash_chain function that: (a) accepts a slice-id argument; (b) reads docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/dispatches/<slice-id>/fixpoint.md; (c) extracts hash-chain entries of the form 'sha256(<reviewer-json-path>)=<hex>'; (d) re-computes SHA-256 over each referenced reviewer JSON file and compares; (e) exits non-zero if any entry is missing, mismatched, or the file is absent. Expose as --check-fixpoint <slice-id> mode. Call it from the --slice dispatch path after check_acc_pin for every prior-merged slice, or maintain a merged-slice registry and iterate. Document exit code 5 for hash-chain failure in the usage block. Until this is implemented, remove the claim 'Closes CRIT-BYPASS-003' from the script header or qualify it as 'hash-chain verification not yet implemented; pending R2 fix-round.'

findings.claim: D-027 in docs/DECISIONS.md records the v0.1 (incorrect) Track 1 sequence, not the v0.2 corrected Scope Y sequence.
findings.evidence: D-027 in docs/DECISIONS.md (line 39) specifies: 'Track 1 (020): 020B → 020B.1 → 020B.2 → 020C → 020C.1 → 020J → 020D1 → 020D2 → [USER-GATE-A].' The D-027 sequence is the exact v0.1 ordering that R1 findings C-CRIT-01 and C-CRIT-02 required to be fixed. The v0.2 plan §3 and §10 D-027 rationale inline both show the correct 12-slice Scope Y sequence, but the binding DECISIONS.md entry was not updated to match.
findings.impact: D-027 is the authoritative governance record for the parallel-track execution protocol. Every Codex dispatch package for a Track 1 slice must include docs/DECISIONS.md in spec_paths (per §4.1 'always includes … the relevant ADOPT-001 sections, and any rule files the slice references'). A Codex executor reading D-027 from DECISIONS.md to validate its dispatch sequence will see 020D2 following immediately after 020D1 — the original ordering bug from v0.1. Any future audit, review agent, or gate check that keys off DECISIONS.md rather than the plan will operate against the wrong Track 1 sequence.
findings.mitigation: Amend D-027 in docs/DECISIONS.md to reflect the corrected Scope Y Track 1 sequence: '020B → 020B.1 → 020B.2 → 020C → 020C.1 → 020J → 020K → 020D1 → 020H part 1 → 020E.a → [USER-GATE-A0] → 020H part 2 → 020D2 → [USER-GATE-A].' findings.evidence: §6 text reads 'blob SHAs of the four dispatcher artefacts' then lists five entries: scripts/codex_dispatch.py, scripts/claude_dispatch.py, schemas/codex_work_package.schema.json, schemas/codex_dispatch_result.schema.json, schemas/sonnet_review_result.schema.json. §9 plan-complete AC repeats 'acc-pin-manifest.json committed with ACC repo HEAD + blob SHAs of the four dispatcher artefacts.' The acc-pin-manifest.json at docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/acc-pin-manifest.json also contains five entries matching §6 exactly. The word 'four' is incorrect in both prose locations.
findings.impact: Cosmetic inconsistency; no functional impact on drift detection or gate enforcement. The manifest itself and the check_acc_pin function both iterate over the actual keys, so the mismatch is a documentation error only.
findings.mitigation: Change 'four dispatcher artefacts' to 'five dispatcher artefacts (two scripts + three schemas)' in both §6 and §9. No changes to the manifest or script needed.

structured_review.summary: All 9 R1 correctness findings (3 CRIT + 4 MAJ + 1 MIN + 1 nit) are verifiably closed in v0.2: slice ordering matches WP-SCP-020 §3 verbatim, 020K is present, 020E.a is correctly described, 020E.b/E.c are explicitly deferred, 020H part 1 content is correct, §4.3 decision table handles APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS(MIN/nit-only), session_id is explicitly not used with FUP filed, PR count is 12, and cost caps are quantified. Two new unmitigated MAJs were introduced in v0.2: (1) the gate-enforcement helper claims to implement 3× APPROVED hash-chain verification to partially close CRIT-BYPASS-003 but contains no such implementation — the check is documented in comments only; (2) D-027 in DECISIONS.md was not updated from the v0.1 incorrect Track 1 sequence, leaving the binding decision record in conflict with the corrected plan §3. One new MIN (gate helper undervalidates USER-GATE-A0 artefact against §9 requirements) and one nit (off-by-one 'four' vs five blob SHAs in §6/§9) are also present. Verdict: CHANGES_REQUESTED.
